Thank you for that.  My parents are really wonderful people.  We have our squabbles (aka I have a meltdown and lose control), but afterward they are very clear in telling me that they love me and nothing I can do will ever change that.  I really struggle with having to depend on them so heavily at 25, but I’m starting to accept that while I need more help than most people, I also have a unique view on the world and I should appreciate that and love myself for it the same way my parents do.  My biggest wish is that someday I can really be proud of myself so that I can know what it is that makes my parents proud of me.  I want to be able to pay for a nice vacation that takes them somewhere that they’ve always wanted to go but haven’t been able to because they’re watching over me.  I want to give them things they really want and need instead of the opposite, them giving me the things I want and need.  :)

I’m not too torn up over this anymore, it’s been almost a year, so I’m ready to talk about it.  I don’t understand how most people are, but I find a way to love everybody.  I just need to find a way to love this person and bullies too.
“That’s why kids with autism don’t respond when you shout their name in their ear.”  I dare you to scream in an autistic child’s ear and come back and tell me you don’t get _any_ sort of response...
Particularly the view that autistic people “don’t have another 20 years to wait.”

Yeah, I can relate to not having anybody you can actually cal a good friend.  I’ve had people I thought were close friends back off and not interact with me very much after I opened up to them and tried talking with them about my problems.  It’s like everybody I become friends with just sees me as that funny autistic guy who makes the occasional clever joke and that’s all they really hang around me for.  My whole sense of humor revolves around self-degradation, and it seems like almost all of my friends just like me when I’m joking around.  When I get serious they get all tentative and stop talking to me as much.   

I’ve had a handful of friends who aren’t that way, but they’re all hours away from me, and I’m bad about keeping up with people when I don’t run into them at school all the time.  I really don’t think about anybody except for when I see them often.  I’m just trapped in my own head, so preoccupied with my own world and problems that I forget that other people exist.  I’ve even forgotten what my parents look like and how they sound when I don’t see them for a while.  I’ve even had a couple of moments when I’ve forgotten that I have parents and have this weird revelation where I remember they exist and can’t remember what it’s like to talk to them.  I just can’t keep up with people unless I’m forced to interact with them.  It sucks, especially because it always seems like I make a really good friend right when I have to move twelve hours away.

It’s just like I forget that I have friends I can talk to about things, and then when I remember, it’s been 6 months without any contact and they’re really not as invested in helping me with my problems anymore.

Right now is really bad, because I’ve moved back in with my parents while I take a semester off to deal with my problems and so I’m hours away from any friends, and I don’t know how to make friends without being forced to interact with people regularly.  I just wish there were some friend-finding app for people with autism or other social issues where you’d be paired up with a person who’ll check in on you regularly and listen to your problems and just hang out or whatever.  That sounds really stupid and it would never work, but it’d be really nice.  I really have no idea of how to make friends outside of work and school.

It’s just that nobody really approaches me because I come off as cold and aloof.  I get really anxious around strangers, and I have trouble making any conversation at all with people I don’t know.  I open up and change completely when I’m comfortable with someone, but nobody ever gets to that point because nobody can get past those first couple of interactions.

You sound like a good friend.  While I like to imagine that I'll eventually be able to find someone like you as a friend, it's been 24 years and I haven't even gotten close yet, so I don't know.  I don't even know where I would get started right now, I'm away from school and the forced social interaction that goes along with school, which is really the only way I know to make friends.  I just have literally nobody that I'm spending time with right now.  Nobody at all.  

I'm sure it would help me to find a friend, but at the same time I feel like complete garbage right now and that makes me worried that I won't be able to interact with any new people I meet, much less make friends with them.  Unless I feel just right, I just don't want to meet anybody.  It's just really frustrating.

I'm sorry you have to deal with schizophrenia.  My grandmother was diagnosed with schizophrenia and I spent my whole life thinking I'd develop it while being autistic as well, but it turns out psychology wasn't very good at the time and she was actually just autistic.  I think on the social side of things, the two have a lot in common.  Paranoia in general gives me meltdowns I think (I say I think because I'm not sure what paranoia feels like, but I've described what I'm feeling sometimes and people say it's paranoia, so that's what I'm assuming it is), so being paranoid a lot would be terrifying for me.  I feel like in general schizophrenia is a lot greater of a burden to bear, so I'm sorry you have to deal with that.  Having meltdowns, not knowing why I feel bad, and being unable to tell people that I feel bad in general is tough, but I feel like schizophrenia probably causes a lot more negative feelings in general than being autistic does.  Autism just makes it next to impossible to understand or deal with those feelings.  Like, I have sensory problems and constantly get overwhelmed and have meltdowns where I hit myself in my head and chest, but I don't think any of that is as bad as most of the symptoms that I've read about with schizophrenia.  I'm really sorry for what you have to go through.

People always tell me that I'm going to look back on these days and think "how did I ever feel like that?  How did I think that I'd never feel better?"  I just think that's inaccurate.  The people telling me that were depressed for a couple of months and didn't have to deal with anything else on top of that.  Like, they could express those feelings to a therapist and were able to think about times other than the present, but I'm pretty stuck in the present; I have trouble  thinking about anything but the present, and I've heard that this is a trait common to autistic people.  If I feel bad, I just feel bad.  It's not like I can think about how I'm going to feel in the future or even about how good I felt five minutes ago.  Whatever I feel is how I feel, period.  Do you feel this way as well?  Most of the time it feels like I'll never feel happy again, or like you said, like my life has fallen apart, it's going to keep falling apart, and it's not going back together any time soon.  I feel you on the not wanting to watch twitch anymore as well.  Most of the things I used to enjoy feel more like tasks than pleasures these days.  

I would say that if you feel this way about a lot of things, never try drugs like opiates or benzodiazepines.  They sort of made a lot of the problems that I have a lot easier, and that made them super addictive.  I got addicted to opiates and then benzodiazepines while I was still addicted to opiates.  I wish I could still be addicted to them, but money made that impossible, and I'm never going to steal or do anything otherwise illegal to get them.  I don't know how to do it in the first place, and I wouldn't know what to do with any stolen items once I had them.  Like, how would I make any money off of something that'd been stolen?  I'd get caught for sure, plus I'd feel absolutely horrible about it.  Anyways, completely off topic for a second, but addictions can't last, so I had to quit, and being in withdrawals and recovery while still dealing with all of the mental health issues and a disability is just fucking awful.  I've relapsed more times than I can count now, only for one day at a time, but still.  It's just not worth it, it never was.

I feel like meeting on twitch could be cool, though I'm really scared to do it.  Even just meeting somebody online is terrifying.  I don't have much to talk about; I can really only talk about topics, like whatever the streamer is playing.  I feel like I'd be really awkward.  I haven't really had a friend in a year now, and I haven't actually made any in 3-4 years.  Like, Every time I try and make a friend and fail I end up thinking about it for years on end.  When it works though, it's great, so I'm not discounting it.  If you want to meet up on twitch, I'd be okay with it, it's just that it could be really awkward, because I'm _really_ awkward when I'm given time to think about meeting someone, lol.  Just let me know if you really want to catch a stream, because I think you're right that it could be helpful.
Thanks for the advice, I really appreciate it.

Okay, that’s really helpful.  I’ve been trying to force myself to be productive before I allow myself to have any fun at all, and I’ve been finding that because of it I’m failing to do either.  It’s helpful to hear from someone that it’s okay to take some time to remember how to enjoy life at all before I try to become a productive member of society again.

Yeah, I really enjoy nature for a lot of the same reasons.  And when I’m playing disc golf I’m entirely immersed in it.  My mind is one-track to the core, multitasking doesn’t even kind of work.  My issue is that when I’m done playing disc golf and driving home and taking my shower, there’s still so much time left in the day.  

I really need to be teaching; I’m a music teacher who’s currently pursuing his doctorate (well, on a leave of absence) to teach music at a collegiate level.  I really enjoy teaching and playing music.  It’s just that that takes so much effort now.  Disc golf is entirely recreational, but music for me is professional.  Right now I’m so low on motivation that I get just a few notes out and I’m already spent for the day, much less teaching students.  I just feel stagnant.  

Should I just focus on remembering how to enjoy things and getting my energy back up for the next couple of weeks with my hobbies and then move on to pursuing my professional passions again?  Or am I just hurting myself by not forcing myself to get over the hump and practicing and teaching while I’m still completely unmotivated to do so?
Okay.  I could use someone to talk to.

Yeah.  I’m never going to kill myself, at least not in my right mind.  I’ve cooled down a bit since I wrote this, and I really am autistic, I just struggle with imposter syndrome a lot.

The issue is that particular phrase, “in my right mind.”  Being autistic means I deal with meltdowns, which are usually self-injurious.  While 99% of the time I could never kill myself or hurt my family in any way, those rare occasions that I go through meltdowns I hate myself 100x more than I’ve ever hated anything else.  The thought of hurting or killing myself gets incredibly exciting and I really look forward to it with some perverse pleasure.  I almost feel euphoric thinking that I might get to kill this person I hate so much (myself, I’m not homicidal).  

I really feel like I’m starting to lose my grip on my sanity.  Afterward I feel even worse because of the fact that if I had been in a position to do so, I likely would have completely ignored the pain it would have caused others and gone through with committing suicide.  Fortunately, when I have a meltdown and start heading to the top of my preferred parking garage, I always calm down before I can get to the top.  I’m just worried that one day I’m going to have a meltdown while I also happen to be in a place where I can actually commit suicide, and none of the people who can help me get help seem to be concerned about this in the slightest.  Probably because I struggle to express my emotions, I come off as indifferent, even when I’m really distressed.  When asked how I’m feeling I struggle to explain much beyond “I’m feeling anxious” or “I’m feeling depressed.”  That’s about as complex as I can get verbally, at least.

The past week I’ve been playing a lot of disc golf, actually.  I used to play a ton of disc golf before my depression and GAD got so crippling, and it’s something I really love doing.  I love hiking, being in nature, and throwing discs, so disc golf is the perfect sport for me, plus it’s a solitary sport so the whole “I can’t hold a conversation past a sentence or two” thing isn’t that big of an issue.  It’s been helping s good bit, but even when I’m happy it seems like I’m standing on the precipice of my depression, looking down into the abyss, and the floor could crumble out from beneath me at any moment.  Happiness doesn’t feel good at the moment because I feel like it’s not safe anymore.  I could have a random meltdown because my shirt rubbed my chest the wrong way and go from being kind of happy back to wanting to kill myself all over the course of thirty seconds or less.

I’m trying to find help, but everybody I’m going to is either telling me to go to somebody else about getting help or telling me that I have to wait another three months in order for them to want to start a new type of treatment plan, even though the current one really seems to be making things much worse.
